nieuw.titel: Keep an unfamiliar tournament army simple
nieuw.tekst: While learning an army or the game, keep the list straightforward: take fewer units to manage and avoid elaborate magic-item combinations or synergies.
nieuw.waarom: The speakers say complexity adds mental work when you are unfamiliar with an army. He chose very few units for his first Old World event to reduce mistakes and make the army more forgiving.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He took one large Grave Guard unit, one large Blood Knights unit, one Zombies unit and four characters while learning Old World.

nieuw.titel: Protect vulnerable flanks with terrain or a board edge
nieuw.tekst: If your army is vulnerable to enemies reaching its flanks or rear, use buildings or impassable terrain as defensive anchors. Alternatively, refuse a flank against a board edge to remove that approach.
nieuw.waarom: He says his three-unit army mostly moved straight ahead and would be in serious trouble if enemies got around or behind it.

nieuw.tekst: With his Vampire Counts setup, keep Mortis Engines hidden behind hills or impassable terrain against heavy artillery. He would be prepared to stay there rather than advance into cannon fire.
nieuw.waarom: He regards shooting as a major weakness of the list and says he cannot protect the Mortis Engines from it unless he hides them.

nieuw.titel: Use Reserve Move magic to accelerate the undead advance
nieuw.tekst: Use magic granting Reserve Move to push Vampire Counts units forward and apply pressure. He combined this with the extra movement provided by two nearby Mortis Engines.
nieuw.waarom: He found that the extra movement could produce a much faster advance and put substantial pressure on an opponent.
nieuw.voorbeeld: With a movement buff, his Grave Guard moved eighteen inches in one turn through two nine-inch moves.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He usually avoided moving that fast because he wanted to keep his army compact and prevent access to its flanks or rear.

nieuw.titel: Consider moderating early wins in battle-point events
nieuw.tekst: At events ranked by battle points, he sometimes deliberately settles for fifteen or sixteen points instead of twenty in the opening round. He aims to reach the leading bracket later rather than immediately.
nieuw.waarom: He says early leaders face capable opponents who often play conservatively, limiting later scores. A player coming from behind can overtake them with a larger win.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He notes that this event instead ranked wins first, with battle points used as the tiebreaker.

nieuw.titel: Accept a small loss rather than force a risky recovery
nieuw.tekst: When slightly behind, consider preserving a small loss instead of launching risky combined charges to recover the score. Take your position in the tournament and the remaining games into account before committing.
nieuw.waarom: He has seen players turn a small deficit into a heavy loss when desperate multiple charges failed.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He describes deciding that an eight-to-twelve loss is safer when two games remain and he is still in a safe tournament bracket.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: If the position is already hopeless, he says there are games where he might as well go for it.
